extracted.intended_audience: appellate practitioners, pro se litigants, and court clerks handling appeals in the D.C. Court of Appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules governing records on appeal, appendices, transcripts, fee waivers (in forma pauperis), computation and extension of time, petitions for review of agency orders, and transmission/filing of records in the D.C. Court of Appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of the Record on Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The record on appeal consists of: (1) the original papers and exhibits filed in the Superior Court; (2) the transcript of proceedings, if any; and (3) a certified copy of the docket entries prepared by the Clerk of the Superior Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the items that must be included to constitute the record on appeal (Rule 10(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant’s Duty to Order Transcript
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 days after filing the notice of appeal, the appellant must either: (A) order from the reporter a transcript of such parts of the proceedings not already on file as the appellant considers necessary and identify any transcript already prepared; or (B) file a certificate in this court stating that no transcript will be ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies unless proceeding under Rule 10(b)(5) (special waiver/CJA provisions). The appellant must also identify transcripts for inclusion in the record (Rule 10(b)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement When Asserting Unsupported Finding or Conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appellant intends to urge on appeal that a finding or conclusion is unsupported by or contrary to the evidence, the appellant must include in the record a transcript of all evidence relevant to that finding or conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Cobb v. Standard Drug Co.; failure to include necessary transcript may foreclose review of such evidentiary challenges (Rule 10(b)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial Transcript Procedures and Designation Timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: When the entire transcript is not ordered: (A) appellant must, within 10 days, file a statement of the issues and serve others with the transcript order/certificate and the statement; (B) within 10 days after service, other parties may designate additional parts to be ordered; (C) if appellant does not order designated parts within 10 days after that designation, the designating party may either order them or move in Superior Court to require the appellant to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These steps govern partial-transcript cases and the timelines for designating and ordering additional parts of the record on appeal (Rule 10(b)(3)(A)-(C)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment Arrangements for Transcripts
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of ordering a transcript, a party must make satisfactory arrangements with the Court Reporter Division for paying the cost of the transcript, except when the party is proceeding under Rule 10(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinary transcript costs are the ordering party’s responsibility unless special waiver/CJA provisions apply (Rule 10(b)(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcript Preparation in Waiver/CJA/PCAN Cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Special rules apply when an appellant has a waiver of fees/costs/security, has counsel appointed under the Criminal Justice Act, or counsel appointed under the Prevention of Child Abuse and Neglect Act: such notices or orders may be treated as encompassing an order for preparation of the reporter’s transcript at government expense or require voucher/approval procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details include: for CJA cases a notice of appeal is considered an order for transcript at government expense; PCAN counsel must secure vouchers from Finance Office; civil waiver cases may require a motion in Superior Court (Rule 10(b)(5)(A)-(C) and related passages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of the Evidence When Transcript Unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: If the transcript is unavailable, the appellant may prepare a statement of the evidence or proceedings from the best available means (including recollection). The statement must be served on all parties, who may object or propose amendments within ten days, and the statement and objections are submitted to the trial judge for settlement and approval. The settled statement is included in the record on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure allows creation of an approved statement of proceedings when a transcript cannot be obtained (Rule 10(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreed Statement as the Record on Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: In place of the record defined in Rule 10(a), parties may prepare, sign, and submit to the trial judge a statement of the case showing how the issues arose and were decided; it must set forth only facts essential to resolution of the issues. If approved by the trial judge (with any additions), it shall be certified to this court as the record on appeal and may be filed in place of the appendix required by Rule 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agreed-statement process can replace the usual record/appendix where parties and judge approve a condensed statement of the case (Rule 10(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction or Modification of the Record
rubrics_metrics.description: If any difference arises about whether the record truly discloses what occurred in the Superior Court, the difference must be submitted to and settled by that court and the record conformed accordingly. Omissions or misstatements material to any party may be corrected and a supplemental record certified and forwarded either (A) on stipulation of the parties, or (B) by the Superior Court before or after the record has been forwarded. All other questions as to form and content of the record must be presented to this court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanisms exist to correct or supplement the record to ensure accuracy before appellate consideration (Rule 10(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant’s Duty to Enable Transmission of the Record
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant filing a notice of appeal must comply with Rule 10(b) and do whatever is necessary to enable the Clerk of the Superior Court to assemble and forward the record. If multiple appeals stem from a judgment or order, the Clerk must assemble a single record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellants must cooperate to ensure timely and correct assembly/transmittal of the record (Rule 11(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter’s Duty to Prepare and File Transcript
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receiving an order for a transcript the reporter must note the date of receipt and expected completion date on the order and send a copy so endorsed to the Clerk of the Superior Court. If the transcript cannot be completed within 60 days, the reporter may request additional time from this court and must notify parties via the Clerk. When complete, the reporter must file it with the Director of the Court Reporter Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters must track and communicate expected completion dates, seek extensions if needed, and file completed transcripts with the Director (Rule 11(b)(1)(A)-(C)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director of Court Reporter Division Duties
rubrics_metrics.description: If all transcripts ordered or designated for appeal have not been completed within 60 days, the Director must retain the partial transcript until transcription of all proceedings has been completed. When completed, the transcript must be placed in chronological sequence, with pages renumbered, and filed with the Clerk of the Superior Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director is responsible for assembling, sequencing, renumbering, and filing transcripts when transcription spans periods (Rule 11(b)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerk of the Superior Court Duties on Completion of Record
rubrics_metrics.description: When the record is complete, the Clerk must prepare an index reasonably identifying and numbering the documents constituting the record, promptly send 4 certified copies of that index and the original reporter’s transcript (if any) to the Clerk of this court, and retain other parts of the record for the parties to use, subject to call by this court. In waived-fee cases the Clerk must prepare and submit 2 copies of the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Clerk’s responsibilities include indexing, forwarding certified copies, retaining originals for parties, and adjusted copy counts for fee-waiver cases (Rule 11(b)(3)(A)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forwarding Supplemental Transcripts After Transmittal
rubrics_metrics.description: In appeals where a reporter’s transcript is filed after transmittal of the certified index, the Clerk of the Superior Court must forward the transcript as a supplemental record on appeal promptly after the Director files it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental transcripts are forwarded to the appellate court to complete the record (Rule 11(b)(3)(B)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record for a Preliminary Motion in the Court of Appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: If, before the record is forwarded, a party files a motion in this court for dismissal, summary reversal/affirmance, release pending appeal, stay/injunction, additional security on a supersedeas bond, or other relief, the Clerk of the Superior Court, upon order of this court, must transmit a preliminary record containing the notices of appeal, the order appealed from, and those parts of the record designated by any party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enables appellate consideration of certain preliminary motions before the full record is transmitted (Rule 11(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents Required in the Appendix (Appellant’s Responsibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant must prepare and file an appendix to the briefs containing: (A) the relevant docket entries in the proceeding below; (B) the relevant pleadings, charge, findings, or opinion; (C) the judgment, order, or decision in question; and (D) other parts of the record to which the parties wish to direct the court’s attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These components define the necessary contents of an appendix accompanying appellate briefs (Rule 30(a)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded Material from the Appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: Memoranda of law filed in the Superior Court should not be included in the appendix unless they have independent relevance. Parts of the record may be relied on by the court or the parties even though not included in the appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid including immaterial lengthy memoranda unless independently relevant; the court can consult the full record as needed (Rule 30(a)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies and Timing for Filing the Appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant must file 4 copies of the appendix with the brief and must serve one copy on counsel for each party separately represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow required copy counts and service obligations when filing the appendix (Rule 30(a)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining the Contents of the Appendix (All Parties’ Responsibilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are encouraged to agree on the contents of the appendix. If no agreement, the appellant must, within 20 days after the Clerk notifies that the record is filed, serve on all other parties a designation of the parts of the record to include and a statement of the issues. Other parties may, within 10 days, designate additional parts; the appellant must include those parts. Parties must not engage in unnecessary designation of parts of the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timelines: 20 days for appellant’s designation; 10 days for others to designate additional parts. Avoid unnecessary designations because the entire record is available to the court (Rule 30(b)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs and Sanctions for the Appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless parties agree otherwise, the appellant must pay the cost of the appendix. If appellant considers parts designated by another party unnecessary, the appellant may so advise that party, which must then advance the cost of including those parts. The cost of the appendix is a taxable cost. If any party causes unnecessary parts of the record to be included, the court may impose the costs of those parts on that party and may impose appropriate sanctions after notice and opportunity to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs may be shifted and sanctions imposed for unreasonably increasing litigation costs by including unnecessary material (Rule 30(b)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Format Requirements for the Appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: The appendix must begin with a table of contents identifying the page at which each part begins; pages must be numbered consecutively; relevant docket entries must follow the table of contents and other parts must follow chronologically. When transcript pages are placed in the appendix, the date of each transcript and the page numbers must be listed on a separate page immediately before the included pages. Omissions in text must be indicated by asterisks. Immaterial formal matters (captions, subscriptions, acknowledgments, etc.) should be omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow precise formatting and pagination rules and indicate omissions to aid the court’s navigation of the appendix (Rule 30(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduction and Filing of Exhibits for the Appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits designated for inclusion may be reproduced in a separate volume(s), suitably indexed. Four copies must be filed with each copy of the appendix, and one copy must be served on counsel for each separately represented party. If a transcript of proceedings before an administrative agency was used in a Superior Court action and designated for inclusion, the transcript must be placed in the appendix as an exhibit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibits may be bound separately but must meet copy and indexing requirements (Rule 30(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal on the Original Record Without an Appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: For good cause shown, the court may excuse a party from producing an appendix, or any part thereof, and permit an appeal to proceed on the original record with any copies of the record, or relevant parts, that the court may order the parties to file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court has discretion to excuse appendix production and allow the appeal on the original record (Rule 30(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix Rules for In Forma Pauperis and Waiver Cases
rubrics_metrics.description: No appendix is required in cases where a party has been granted a waiver of fees, costs, or security or counsel has been appointed. However: (1) the appellant must file with the brief 4 copies of any opinion, findings of fact, and conclusions of law (written or set forth orally in the transcript) that relate to the issues raised on appeal; and (2) the appellee may file with the brief 4 copies of any portions of the record to be called to the court's attention that were not furnished by the appellant. A copy of these documents must be served on counsel for each party separately represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when no appendix is required due to waiver, parties must still file specified portions (Rule 30(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computing Time – Excluding Day of Event
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude the day of the act, event, or default that begins the period when computing any period of time specified in these rules or in any court order or applicable statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the basic starting rule for time computation (Rule 26(a)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computing Time – Excluding Intermediate Weekends/Holidays
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude intermediate Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays when the period is less than 11 days, unless an applicable statute or court order provides otherwise, or unless the period is stated in calendar days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this rule for short periods under 11 days; for periods stated in calendar days do not exclude weekends/holidays (Rule 26(a)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computing Time – Including Last Day
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the last day of the period unless it is a Saturday, Sunday, legal holiday, or — if the act is filing a paper in court — a day on which weather or other conditions cause the Clerk’s office to be closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the last day falls on a non-business day or the Clerk’s office is closed, the period extends to the next business day (Rule 26(a)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Legal Holiday for Time Computation
rubrics_metrics.description: For computing time, 'legal holiday' includes New Year’s Day, Martin Luther King, Jr.’s Birthday, Presidents’ Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day, Veterans’ Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day, and any other day appointed as a holiday by the President or the Congress of the United States, or by the District of Columbia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this explicit list (and any other appointed days) when applying Rule 26(a)(2)-(3) (Rule 26(a)(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extending Time – Court May Grant for Good Cause; Exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: For good cause, the court may extend the time prescribed by these rules to perform any act or permit an act after time expires. But the court may not extend the time to file a notice of appeal (except as authorized in Rule 4) or an application for allowance of appeal; to file a petition for review; or for doing any act when the time for doing the act has been prescribed by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are broadly available for good cause but expressly cannot circumvent statutory or specially protected time limits (Rule 26(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Time After Certain Kinds of Service
rubrics_metrics.description: When a party is required or permitted to act within a period after a paper is served on that party, 5 calendar days are added to the prescribed period unless the paper is delivered on the date of service stated in the proof of service. Electronic service is treated as delivered on the date of service stated in the proof. Rule 26(c) does not apply when an order of this court prescribes the time or to notices of appeal under Rules 4, 5, or 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule gives a 5-day cushion after service (subject to exceptions) and specifies treatment of electronic service (Rule 26(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Review – Filing Requirements and Time Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Review of an agency order or decision is commenced by filing with the Clerk an original and six copies of a petition for review. Unless an applicable statute provides a different time frame, the petition must be filed within 30 days after notice of the order or decision is given in conformance with the agency's rules. If the order was made out of the presence of the parties and notice is by mail, petitioner has 5 additional days from the date of mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules apply to Office of Administrative Hearings decisions; Form 5 is a suggested petition form. Filing by mail is not timely unless received by the Clerk within the prescribed time (Rule 15(a)(1)-(2), (5), (8)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Review – Naming Parties and Agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for OAH cases governed separately, the petition must name each party seeking review (using actual names, not terms like 'et al.'), name the agency as respondent, and specify the order or decision or part thereof to be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precise naming is required in the caption or body to effectively name parties (Rule 15(a)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Review – Cross-Petition Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a timely petition for review is filed by a party, any other party to the agency proceeding may file a cross-petition for review within 14 days after the petition was filed, or within 30 days of the date of the challenged order or decision, whichever period expires later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows other agency participants to seek review on an aligned timeline (Rule 15(a)(7)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of Time for Filing Petition for Review After Agency Reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party timely files a petition for rehearing or reconsideration in accordance with the agency rules, the time to petition for review runs from the date when notice of the order denying the petition is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness for judicial review is tolled pending agency reconsideration and restarts on denial notice (Rule 15(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of the Petition for Review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Clerk must serve a copy of the petition for review on each respondent agency and on the Office of the Attorney General for the District of Columbia or other counsel representing any agency respondent. At the time of filing, the petitioner must serve, or have served, a copy on each party admitted to participate in the agency proceedings (except agency respondents) and file a list of those so served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing and service obligations are strict; the petitioner must file a list of parties served (Rule 15(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention in Agency Review Cases
rubrics_metrics.description: A party to the agency proceeding who wants to intervene in this court must, within 30 days from the date the petition is filed, serve upon all parties and file with the Clerk a copy of a notice of intention to intervene, in which case the party will be deemed an intervenor. Any other person who wants to intervene must file a motion to intervene within 30 days of the petition filing (unless extended for good cause). The motion must contain a concise statement of the moving party's interest and the grounds and must state on which side the party seeks to intervene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intervention timelines and procedural content requirements are prescribed (Rule 15(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees When Filing Petition for Review
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing any separate or joint petition for review, the petitioner must pay the Clerk all required fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee obligations apply to petitions for review unless other rule/statute provides otherwise (Rule 15(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Duty to File the Record and Time for Filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent agency must file the record within 60 days after being served with a petition for review. For OAH decisions, the Office of Administrative Hearings must file the record within 60 days of an order directing filing. The court may shorten or extend these deadlines for good cause. The Clerk must notify all parties and intervenors that the record has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default 60-day filing period with court discretion to modify for good cause (Rule 17(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: What Constitutes Filing of the Record by the Agency
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency must file (A) the original or a certified copy of the record on review or parts designated by the parties; or (B) if a partial record is filed, a certified list adequately describing all documents, transcripts, exhibits, and other material constituting the record on review. Parties may stipulate in writing that no record or certified list be filed; the date the stipulation is filed is treated as the date the record is filed. The agency must retain any portion of the record not filed; those parts are part of the record on review and must be sent to the court if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may file full records, partial records with certified lists, or comply with a stipulation; retained portions remain part of the record and must be made available on request (Rule 17(b)(1)-(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of Fees – General Standard Reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The standards governing eligibility for waiver (in forma pauperis) are listed in D.C. Code § 15-712(a)(1)(A)-(D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 24 references statutory criteria for eligibility and then prescribes procedures for appeals and other filings under the waiver regime (Rule 24(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals from Superior Court with Prior Waiver or Court-Appointed Counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: A party who was granted a waiver of court fees, costs, or security in the Superior Court, or determined by the Superior Court to be eligible for court-appointed counsel under relevant statutes, may proceed on appeal without paying fees, costs, or security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior Superior Court determinations carry forward to appellate proceedings (Rule 24(b)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications for Waiver to be Filed in the Superior Court (Procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as stated in Rule 24(b)(1), a party in the Superior Court seeking to take an appeal without paying fees, costs, or security must file in the Superior Court within the time for filing an appeal: (i) a notice of appeal containing the information in Form 1 or Form 2; and (ii) an application to waive court fees, costs, or security pursuant to Superior Court Rule of Civil Procedure 54-II. If the Superior Court grants the waiver, the party may proceed on appeal without paying fees, costs, or security. If the Superior Court denies the waiver in whole or in part, the party may request a hearing under the Superior Court rule, and if denied after the hearing, may file in this court an application to proceed without paying fees, costs, or security (see Form 7) including specified documents and statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must include the notice, the Superior Court waiver application and order, a Form 7 declaration, statement of reasons why Superior Court's denial is in error, and any additional evidence of inability to proceed without hardship (Rule 24(b)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications to be Filed in the Court of Appeals after Paying Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party seeks to proceed on appeal without paying fees after having filed a notice of appeal and paid the required fees, the party must file with this court an application to waive fees/costs/security using Form 7 and sign the declaration contained therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the post-payment route to request waiver from the appellate court (Rule 24(b)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver Applications in Agency Petitions and Extraordinary Writs
rubrics_metrics.description: When review of an order/decision in an agency proceeding proceeds directly to this court, a party may file, along with the petition for review, an application to waive fees/costs/security (Form 7) and sign the declaration contained therein within the time permitted for seeking review. Similarly, a party filing a petition for an extraordinary writ and desiring to proceed without paying fees must file Form 7 and sign the declaration along with the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits fee-waiver applications to accompany direct petitions for review and extraordinary writs (Rule 24(c) and (d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for Deciding Waiver Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 5 calendar days after receiving a completed waiver application, the court must decide whether to approve the application. The Clerk, if authorized, may grant waiver applications. If the court has not ruled within 5 calendar days after receipt of a completed application, the application will be deemed approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a prompt-decision rule with a deemed-approval default if the court does not act within five days, subject to exceptions when additional information is required under statute (Rule 24(e)(1)-(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of Waiver Application and Right to Hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a waiver application is denied by this court, the court shall state the reasons for the denial or partial denial in writing. A party denied a waiver may request a hearing under D.C. Code § 15-712(c)(3)(A); the hearing must be held no later than 14 days after the court receives the hearing request. If after the hearing the waiver is denied, the party must pay the required filing fee within the time specified in the final order of denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written reasons and prompt hearing opportunity are required on denial, with an obligation to pay fees if the denial is sustained (Rule 24(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Merits of Appeal Not Considered in Waiver Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: In considering a waiver application, the court must not consider the merits of the appeal or petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility decisions focus on financial inability/hardship and procedural criteria, not substantive merits (Rule 24(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion for Free Transcripts or Other Documents – Civil Cases
rubrics_metrics.description: A party in a civil case who has been granted a waiver may file a motion in the Superior Court requesting free transcripts or other documents be prepared and explaining the basis for the motion. The Superior Court must grant the motion unless the request is frivolous. In making this determination, the Superior Court must resolve doubt about frivolousness in favor of the applicant. The Superior Court may order that only those portions of the transcripts or other documents necessary to resolution of the appeal or petition be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil fee-waiver applicants have a presumptive right to free transcripts unless the request is frivolous; court should narrowly tailor the transcripts provided (Rule 24(h)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion for Free Transcripts or Other Documents – Criminal Cases
rubrics_metrics.description: In criminal cases where the appellant has been permitted to proceed under the Criminal Justice Act, the notice of appeal will be considered by the Superior Court as encompassing an order for preparation of the reporter’s transcript at government expense. In any other criminal case, a defendant granted a waiver of costs/fees/security may file a motion in the Superior Court requesting free transcripts or other documents; such a motion will be considered an order for preparation of the reporter’s transcript at government expense and will be addressed under procedures established in Rule 10(b)(5)(B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CJA and other criminal-waiver situations trigger government-funded transcript procedures, with reference to Rule 10(b)(5)(B) for applicable procedures (Rule 24(h)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of Waiver Applications and Financial Information
rubrics_metrics.description: The court must keep confidential an application and any financial information submitted by the applicant pursuant to this rule or Superior Court Rule 54-II, except to the court, the litigant, persons authorized by the litigant, or by court order. The application must not be served on the other party. The court’s decision on an application for a waiver shall not be confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications and financial disclosures are confidential except to specified persons; the ultimate decision is public (Rule 24(i)(1) and (3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion for Access to Confidential Waiver Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person seeking access to an application or any financial information provided to the court may file a motion, with notice to the litigant who filed the application, supported by a declaration showing good cause why the confidential information should be released. Any person granted access must not reveal any information contained in the application or financial information except as authorized by law or court order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access is available only on a showing of good cause and includes non-disclosure obligations for those granted access (Rule 24(i)(2)(A)-(B)).
